content: Healthcare providers should actively screen individuals diagnosed with diabetes for potential sleep health issues. These issues may include difficulties in falling or staying asleep due to symptoms of diabetes, the demands of diabetes management, or anxiety related to maintaining appropriate blood glucose levels. When such issues are identified, it is advisable to refer these patients to specialists in sleep medicine or behavioral health professionals for further evaluation and management. Patients with diabetes should be encouraged to adopt habits that promote better sleep. These practices include maintaining a consistent sleep schedule and avoiding caffeine consumption in the afternoon. Such measures can help improve sleep quality and contribute to better overall health outcomes.
